subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the value of k if the length of the tangent from (5,4) to x² + y² + 2ky = 0 is 1.

insider_note: There is no x term and no constant term in the circle, so S₁₁ is short — but the 2k must still be halved into f before anything else, and 2f y₁ then puts the 2 back.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the tangent length as √S₁₁
steps.margin_note: One mark. S₁₁ is the left side of the circle equation with the point substituted, nothing more.
steps.memory_tip: Length of the tangent from P to S = 0 is √S₁₁.
lines: Length of the tangent from (5, 4) to
steps.why: The square of the tangent length from an external point is S₁₁, the whole left side of the circle equation evaluated at that point. Squaring first removes the root before any substitution.
common_mistakes: Using √(g² + f² − c) in place of S₁₁.
Forgetting to square and leaving the root in.

steps.label: Square and solve for k
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 2k(4) = 8k, so the k term carries a factor 8, not 4.
steps.why: Substituting the point directly into x² + y² + 2ky gives 41 + 8k. Setting that equal to 1 leaves one linear equation, and the answer is negative because 41 is already far above 1.
